---
title: How photosynthesis works
lang: en
free: true
---

Photosynthesis is how plants, algae and some bacteria turn light into chemical energy. It is the process that ultimately feeds almost all life on Earth and fills the air with oxygen.

## Capturing light

Inside leaf cells, structures called chloroplasts hold the green pigment chlorophyll. Chlorophyll absorbs mostly red and blue light and reflects green, which is why leaves look green. The captured light energy is used to split water molecules, releasing oxygen as a by-product.

## Making sugar

In a second set of reactions the plant uses that energy to combine carbon dioxide from the air into sugars. This carbon-fixing cycle stores the sun's energy in glucose, which the plant later burns for growth or stores as starch.

So a leaf is really a small solar factory: water and carbon dioxide go in, sunlight powers the machinery, and sugar and oxygen come out.
